main_text.p: tent. Vt Ionæ solatio esse potuit, quòd mare,ipso è naui præcipitato,quieturum præsciret.

5. Erumpit itaq; in charitatis ἀπολείμμα[?] fides, dum fic apud homines urget exe cutione iudicij diuini, ut interim aliorum incolumitati gratuletur eam prænunci- ando. Quibus hoc præstare datum est,ij reuera fide mūdum uicerunt.iuxta illud: Hæc est uictoria quæ uicit mūdum,nem- pe fides noftra. Quis est qui uincit mūn- dum, nisi qui credit Iesum esse filiū Dei? 1.Ioan.5.4.5.

6. Solicitè autem cauere solet, ne cui- quam periculo sit: quòd malit aliorum caussa plurimum laborare & pati, quàm suo nomine cuiquam malè esse. Atq; eo nomine dicitur, διʼ ἀγάπης ἐνεργουμένη[?], per charitatem agens. Gal.5.6.

7. Coronidis uice hoc addam,aliud ef- fe,si cui fides αὐθαίρετος huius [illegible, ~4 letters]odi de sei- pso sententiâ dictet: al[illegible, ~8 letters] dolore extorquear[illegible, ~6 letters] dolorū (ut ipsis [illegible, ~6 letters] posfit. Huius memor[illegible, ~10 letters] ci[illegible, ~8 letters]

page.notes: The lower part of the page, from paragraph 7 onward, is covered by a hand and a pen, so most of those lines are illegible. The Greek in paragraphs 5 and 6 is partly obscured and marked [?]. The "II" marks in the lower right are a background grid, not printed text, and are left out. No marginal notes are visible on this page.
